title: Management by Objectives Explained | Principles of Management Ep 20
description:
What happens when a manager only gives orders? In this animated lesson, Ravi now runs two Chai Corner outlets, and Meena runs outlet 2. Every morning Ravi hands her a new order. Meena never gets a say, her motivation drops, and at month end nobody knows if she did well.

You will learn what Management by Objectives (MBO) means: the manager and the worker agree on clear, measurable goals together, review progress regularly, and judge the work by its results. MBO was made famous by Peter Drucker in his 1954 book The Practice of Management, where he called it "management by objectives and self-control". We walk through the 5 steps of MBO (set organizational objectives, set individual objectives together, make action plans, review progress, appraise and reward), using Ravi's SMART goal from Episode 15: 500 cups a day at outlet 2 by March. Then we cover the benefits of MBO (clarity, motivation, participation) and its limitations (it takes time, and it can focus too much on numbers).

This is Episode 20 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
